docs.title: Unify Customer Identities Directly Inside Your Data Warehouse
docs.text:
Production-grade deterministic graph resolution, blocking-based fuzzy super-clustering, golden profile survivorship, persistent cluster IDs, and GDPR erasure across DuckDB, Snowflake, BigQuery, and Databricks. Zero data movement. 100% SQL-auditable.

Get Started in 60 Seconds → Explore Architecture GitHub Repository

docs.title: ⚡ 60-Second Quickstart
docs.text:
Run a complete synthetic multi-source identity resolution pipeline locally on DuckDB:

# 1. Install with DuckDB, Web UI, and MCP extras
pip install "sql-identity-resolution[duckdb,ui,mcp]"

# 2. Run the 10,000-row synthetic quickstart demo
idr quickstart --rows 10000 --output demo.duckdb

# 3. Launch the interactive React Web UI & Cluster Explorer
idr ui --db demo.duckdb

docs.title: 🏗️ Enterprise Capabilities Built In
docs.text:
🔗 Deterministic + Fuzzy Graph Engine

Anchor-based star edges ($N-1$ edges per group) prevent $O(N^2)$ clique explosion, paired with iterative Label Propagation and optional blocking-key fuzzy super-clustering.

🧼 Domain Canonicalizers & Custom SQL

Built-in normalizers (EMAIL_STANDARD, EMAIL_STRIP_PLUS, PHONE_DIGITS, PHONE_US_10, ALPHANUMERIC_UPPER) plus custom warehouse SQL templates via {val}.

🛡️ Poison-Pill Exclusions & Guardrails

Built-in blocklist (use_default_exclusions: true), wildcard ANY rules, warehouse-table exclusions, and max_group_size thresholds stop bad data from creating mega-clusters.

📌 Persistent Resolved IDs & Crosswalk

"Largest Cluster Wins" stabilization preserves existing resolved_id values across incremental runs and logs every cluster merge or split into idr_out.resolved_id_crosswalk.

⚖️ Manual Stewardship Overrides

Override graph links with FORCE_LINK, DO_NOT_LINK, and ISOLATE via YAML, SQL (idr_meta.identity_override), Web UI Explorer, or dbt_idr seeds.

🗑️ GDPR / CCPA Right-to-be-Forgotten

Purge entities or identifier values across all output and staging tables with idr privacy forget while recording an immutable compliance receipt in idr_meta.privacy_audit_log.

docs.title: Core Concepts & 8-Stage Pipeline Architecture
docs.text: This guide explains the foundational data model and the 8-stage execution engine that powers sql-identity-resolution.

docs.title: 1. Core Building Blocks
docs.text:
Every source table registered in idr_meta.source_table defines four distinct concepts:

Concept Role in the Pipeline Example entity_key Globally unique composite primary key (<table_id>:<raw_key>) identifying a single row from a source table as a graph node. 'crm:10042', 'orders:98112' watermark_column Timestamp or monotonically increasing column used in INCR runs to extract new/updated rows since last_watermark_value. Optional (tables without a watermark use state-diffing). updated_at, order_date Identifiers (idr_meta.source_identifier) Match keys extracted, canonicalized, and filtered against exclusions to build deterministic graph edges between entities. EMAIL, PHONE, LOYALTY_ID, CUSTOMER_ID Attributes (idr_meta.entity_attribute_mapping) Descriptive profile columns used after graph resolution to build the Golden Profile (idr_out.golden_profile_current) via survivorship rules (and optionally evaluated by fuzzy blocking rules). first_name, last_name, lifetime_value, country_code

[!IMPORTANT] Identifiers vs. Attributes: - Identifiers decide which records belong to the same person (Graph Connectivity). - Attributes decide which profile values win for that person (Golden Record Survivorship).

docs.title: 2. The 8-Stage Execution Pipeline
docs.text:
Whether triggered via idr run, the Web UI (POST /api/setup/run), MCP (run_pipeline), or IDRRunner.run(), the engine executes 8 deterministic stages in sequence and emits real-time telemetry via progress_callback:

flowchart TD
    S1["Stage 1: preflight\nAuto-upgrade SYSTEM_TABLES & validate source columns"] --> S2
    S2["Stage 2: entity_extraction\nExtract delta rows + candidate expansion (or FULL scan)"] --> S3
    S3["Stage 3: identifier_extraction\nApply Domain Canonicalizers, Exclusions & No-Watermark State-Diff"] --> S4
    S4["Stage 4: attribute_extraction\nMaterialize entity_attributes (skipped automatically if 0 fuzzy rules)"] --> S5
    S5["Stage 5: edge_building\nApply ISOLATE, build N-1 Anchor Edges, apply DO_NOT_LINK & FORCE_LINK"] --> S6
    S6["Stage 6: label_propagation\nIterative connected components + Persistent resolved_id stabilization"] --> S7
    S7["Stage 7: fuzzy_matching\nBlocking-key similarity super-clustering (when fuzzy_rules active)"] --> S8
    S8["Stage 8: output_generation\nUpdate membership, confidence scores, golden profiles, crosswalk & watermarks"]

docs.title: Stage 1: preflight (PreflightStage)
docs.text:
• Automatically upgrades existing warehouse schemas by checking SYSTEM_TABLES (_ensure_schema_upgrades) and creating any newly introduced tables (idr_meta.identity_override, idr_meta.privacy_audit_log, idr_out.resolved_id_crosswalk, etc.) without requiring a manual reset.
  • Verifies that idr_meta.source_table and idr_meta.rule are populated and validates that every configured entity_key_expr, watermark_column, identifier expression, and attribute expression exists in the physical source tables.

docs.title: Stage 2: entity_extraction (ExtractionStage.extract_entities)
docs.text:
• FULL Mode: Extracts all entities (WHERE 1=1) from active source tables into idr_work.entities_delta.
  • INCR Mode:
  • For tables with a watermark_column: filters WHERE <watermark_column> > <last_watermark_value> (minus optional watermark_lookback_minutes).
  • For tables without a watermark_column: scans all rows (WHERE 1=1) and marks the table for Stage 3 identifier state-diffing so in-place UPDATEs to existing rows are caught while unchanged rows are pruned before candidate expansion.

docs.title: Stage 3: identifier_extraction (ExtractionStage.extract_identifiers)
docs.text:
• Applies the rule's configured Domain Canonicalizer (EMAIL_STANDARD, EMAIL_STRIP_PLUS, PHONE_DIGITS, PHONE_US_10, ALPHANUMERIC_UPPER, LOWERCASE, UPPERCASE, EXACT/NONE, or custom inline SQL {val}) to produce identifier_value_norm.
  • Excludes poison-pill identifiers matching idr_meta.identifier_exclusion (supporting both specific identifier_type and wildcard ANY / * rules, with case-insensitive EXACT and LIKE matching).
  • No-Watermark State-Diffing (INCR mode):
  • Compares extracted (entity_key, identifier_type, identifier_value_norm) tuples from no-watermark tables against idr_out.identity_identifiers_current.
  • Any entity whose identifier set is 100% identical to the previous run is pruned from idr_work.entities_delta and idr_work.identifiers_extracted.
  • Candidate Expansion (INCR mode):
  • Pulls in historical entities from idr_out.identity_identifiers_current and idr_out.identity_resolved_membership_current that share an identifier or cluster with the newly changed delta entities (watermark_value = NULL), ensuring entire impacted connected components are re-evaluated accurately.
  • Zero-Delta Short-Circuit:
  • If 0 newly changed entities remain after watermark filtering and state-diffing, IDRRunner short-circuits Stages 4–8 and completes in seconds.

docs.title: Stage 4: attribute_extraction (ExtractionStage.extract_attributes)
docs.text:
• When active fuzzy_rules exist, extracts mapped attributes for delta entities into idr_work.entity_attributes.
  • Zero-Fuzzy Optimization: When 0 active fuzzy rules are configured, Stage 4 skips materializing idr_work.entity_attributes entirely (saving tens of millions of intermediate row writes on large datasets) because Stage 8's ProfileBuilder queries source tables directly.

docs.title: Stage 5: edge_building (GraphStage.build_edges)
docs.text:
1. Pre-Edge Overrides (ISOLATE): Removes any entity listed as ISOLATE in idr_meta.identity_override from idr_work.identifiers_all so it never forms edges.
  2. Anchor-Based Star Edges ($N-1$ Edges):
  3. Groups idr_work.identifiers_all by (identifier_type, identifier_value_norm).
  4. Filters out groups where COUNT(*) > max_group_size (logging oversized groups to idr_out.skipped_identifier_groups).
  5. Connects every member of a valid group to MIN(entity_key) (anchor_key), producing $N-1$ edges instead of $\frac{N(N-1)}{2}$ edges.
  6. Post-Edge Overrides (DO_NOT_LINK & FORCE_LINK):
  7. DO_NOT_LINK: Deletes direct edges between (entity_key_a, entity_key_b) and detaches MAX(entity_key_a, entity_key_b) from any shared identifier anchor group containing MIN(entity_key_a, entity_key_b).
  8. FORCE_LINK: Injects an explicit MANUAL_OVERRIDE edge between (entity_key_a, entity_key_b) and ensures both entities are registered in idr_work.entities_delta.

docs.title: Stage 6: label_propagation (GraphStage.label_propagation)
docs.text:
• Builds undirected edges (lp_edges) over active connected nodes and iteratively propagates MIN(candidate_label) across neighbors until changes == 0 (or max_iters is reached).
  • Re-attaches singleton entities (entities with zero incident edges) with label = entity_key.
  • Executes Persistent resolved_id Stabilization (_stabilize_resolved_ids) so existing cluster IDs are preserved across runs.

docs.title: Stage 7: fuzzy_matching (GraphStage.fuzzy_matching)
docs.text: • Evaluates active rules in idr_meta.fuzzy_rule over deterministic clusters using blocking keys (blocking_key_expr) and similarity expressions (score_expr >= threshold), merging matching clusters via a second label propagation pass.

docs.title: Stage 8: output_generation (OutputStage.generate_outputs)
docs.text:
• Updates idr_out.identity_resolved_membership_current and idr_out.identity_identifiers_current.
  • Records any old_resolved_id -> new_resolved_id transitions into idr_out.resolved_id_crosswalk.
  • Computes cluster-level confidence scores (confidence_score, edge_diversity, match_density, primary_reason) in idr_out.identity_clusters_current.
  • Builds idr_out.golden_profile_current via ProfileBuilder using configured survivorship strategies (PRIORITY, RECENCY, FREQUENCY).
  • Updates idr_meta.run_state watermarks using WHERE watermark_value IS NOT NULL so candidate-expanded historical rows (watermark_value = NULL) never overwrite last_watermark_value.

docs.title: 3. Persistent resolved_id Stabilization & Crosswalk
docs.text:
In naive graph pipelines, resolved_id is simply MIN(entity_key) of each connected component. If crm:500 and orders:600 initially form cluster crm:500, and a new record ads:100 arrives tomorrow, MIN(entity_key) would flip the entire cluster's ID from crm:500 to ads:100—breaking downstream BI dashboards, reverse ETL syncs, and feature stores.

sql-identity-resolution solves this with Cross-Run resolved_id Stabilization (GraphStage._stabilize_resolved_ids):

  1. New Entities Joining an Existing Cluster:
  2. When new entities connect to an existing cluster from idr_out.identity_resolved_membership_current, the cluster retains its existing resolved_id regardless of whether the new entity key is lexicographically smaller.
  3. Two Existing Clusters Merging ("Largest Cluster Wins"):
  4. When a new bridge identifier merges two previously separate clusters ($C_1$ and $C_2$), the largest previous cluster's resolved_id wins (ORDER BY prev_size DESC, prev_created_at ASC, prev_resolved_id ASC).
  5. Cluster Splits:
  6. If an override (DO_NOT_LINK or ISOLATE) splits an existing cluster into two components, only one component may claim the historical resolved_id (preferring the component containing the anchor entity key), while the split-off component receives a fresh canonical ID.
  7. Audit Crosswalk (idr_out.resolved_id_crosswalk):
  8. Every time an entity's old_resolved_id transitions to a new_resolved_id (e.g., the smaller cluster in a merge adopting the larger cluster's resolved_id), Stage 8 writes an immutable mapping row to idr_out.resolved_id_crosswalk(run_id, old_resolved_id, new_resolved_id, entity_key, change_type, changed_at).

docs.title: Configuration, Canonicalizers & Enterprise Governance
docs.text: sql-identity-resolution is configured declaratively via YAML (idr apply-config) or interactively through the Web UI Setup Wizard. All configuration state lives in idr_meta.* tables inside your warehouse.

docs.title: 1. Complete YAML Manifest Reference
docs.text:
# Enable built-in poison-pill identifier exclusions (noreply@, test@, 0000000000, etc.)
use_default_exclusions: true

# 1. Source Tables
sources:
  - id: crm
    table: raw.crm_customers
    entity_key: customer_id
    entity_type: PERSON
    watermark_column: updated_at
    watermark_lookback_minutes: 0
    identifiers:
      - type: EMAIL
        expr: email
      - type: PHONE
        expr: phone
    attributes:
      - name: first_name
        expr: first_name
      - name: last_name
        expr: last_name
      - name: email
        expr: email
      - name: phone
        expr: phone
      - name: record_updated_at
        expr: updated_at

  - id: loyalty_lookup
    table: raw.loyalty_cards
    entity_key: card_id
    entity_type: PERSON
    # Omit watermark_column if the table has no timestamp;
    # INCR runs will scan all rows and state-diff identifiers automatically.
    identifiers:
      - type: EMAIL
        expr: member_email
      - type: LOYALTY
        expr: loyalty_number
    attributes: []

# 2. Deterministic Matching Rules
rules:
  - id: email_standard_match
    type: EXACT
    match_keys: [EMAIL]
    canonicalize: EMAIL_STANDARD
    priority: 1
    max_group_size: 10000

  - id: phone_us10_match
    type: EXACT
    match_keys: [PHONE]
    canonicalize: PHONE_US_10
    priority: 2
    max_group_size: 5000

  - id: loyalty_custom_sql
    type: EXACT
    match_keys: [LOYALTY]
    # Custom inline SQL canonicalizer using {val} placeholder
    canonicalize: "REGEXP_REPLACE(UPPER(TRIM({val})), '^0+', '')"
    priority: 3
    max_group_size: 100

# 3. Optional Probabilistic Fuzzy Rules (Post-Deterministic Super-Clustering)
fuzzy_rules:
  - id: fuzzy_name_match
    name: First + Last Name Jaro-Winkler
    blocking_key: "CONCAT(SOUNDEX(last_name), '_', SUBSTR(UPPER(first_name), 1, 1))"
    score_expr:
      default: "idr_meta.jaro_winkler_similarity(<a>, <b>)"
      bigquery: "1.0 - SAFE_DIVIDE(CAST(EDIT_DISTANCE(<a>, <b>) AS FLOAT64), CAST(GREATEST(LENGTH(<a>), LENGTH(<b>), 1) AS FLOAT64))"
    threshold: 0.88
    priority: 100

# 4. Golden Profile Survivorship Rules
survivorship:
  - attribute: email
    strategy: PRIORITY
    source_priority: [crm, loyalty_lookup]
    recency_field: record_updated_at

  - attribute: first_name
    strategy: RECENCY
    recency_field: record_updated_at

  - attribute: phone
    strategy: FREQUENCY
    recency_field: record_updated_at

# 5. Custom Identifier Exclusions (Supplementing use_default_exclusions)
exclusions:
  - type: EMAIL
    value: "%@internal-corp.com"
    match: LIKE
    reason: Internal employee emails
  - type: ANY
    value: "REDACTED"
    match: EXACT
    reason: Masked compliance value across all identifier types

# 6. Manual Stewardship Overrides
overrides:
  - type: FORCE_LINK
    entity_key_a: "crm:1001"
    entity_key_b: "loyalty_lookup:5099"
    reason: Verified VIP account merge
  - type: DO_NOT_LINK
    entity_key_a: "crm:1001"
    entity_key_b: "crm:2044"
    reason: Shared family phone number — distinct individuals
  - type: ISOLATE
    entity_key_a: "crm:9999"
    reason: Shared store kiosk account — never merge

docs.title: 2. Built-In Domain Canonicalizers & Custom SQL
docs.text:
Each deterministic rule in rules specifies a canonicalize strategy (idr_core/canonicalizers.py and dbt_idr/models/staging/stg_identifiers.sql). You can choose from 9 built-in cross-warehouse canonicalizers or write custom inline warehouse SQL:

Canonicalizer Name Behavior Example Input → Normalized Output EMAIL_STANDARD Trims, lowercases, and strips dots (.) from the local part of @gmail.com / @googlemail.com addresses while preserving +tag aliases. ' John.Doe+vip@Gmail.com ' → 'johndoe+vip@gmail.com' EMAIL_STRIP_PLUS Performs all EMAIL_STANDARD normalizations plus strips +tag sub-addressing from the local part across all email domains. 'John.Doe+promo@gmail.com' → 'johndoe@gmail.com' PHONE_DIGITS Strips all non-numeric characters ([^0-9]); returns NULL if fewer than 7 digits remain. '+1 (800) 555-0199' → '18005550199' PHONE_US_10 Strips non-digits, removes a leading US country code 1 from 11-digit numbers, and returns the 10-digit subscriber number (or NULL if < 7 digits). '+1 (415) 555-2671' → '4155552671' ALPHANUMERIC_UPPER Uppercases and strips all non-alphanumeric characters ([^A-Z0-9]). Ideal for loyalty cards, VINs, and tax/device IDs. 'vip-9901 a' → 'VIP9901A' LOWERCASE LOWER(TRIM(val)) ' Alice@Example.com ' → 'alice@example.com' UPPERCASE UPPER(TRIM(val)) 'abc-123' → 'ABC-123' EXACT / NONE TRIM(val) (preserves case and internal punctuation) ' Token_AbC ' → 'Token_AbC' Custom SQL ({val}) Any SQL expression containing {val} (where {val} is replaced by CAST(<identifier_expr> AS VARCHAR)). "REGEXP_REPLACE(LOWER(TRIM({val})), '^0+', '')"

docs.title: 3. Poison-Pill Exclusions (idr_meta.identifier_exclusion)
docs.text:
Bad placeholder identifiers (null, unknown, 0000000000, noreply@...) can link thousands of unrelated customers into a single giant cluster. sql-identity-resolution provides three layers of protection:

  1. Built-In Default Exclusion Library (use_default_exclusions: true):
  2. Seeds 30+ battle-tested exclusions across ANY (null, none, n/a, na, unknown, tbd, test, dummy, anonymous, redacted, 0, -1), EMAIL (%@example.%, %@test.%, %@mailinator.com, noreply@%, no-reply@%, donotreply@%, info@%, support@%, admin@%, sales@%, billing@%), and PHONE (0000000000–9999999999, 1234567890, 11234567890, 0000000).
  3. Custom YAML Exclusions:
  4. Add domain-specific patterns under exclusions: with type (EMAIL, PHONE, or ANY / * for all types) and match (EXACT or LIKE).
  5. Direct Warehouse Table Management:
  6. Data stewards or upstream ETL jobs can insert rows directly into idr_meta.identifier_exclusion without touching YAML: 
    INSERT INTO idr_meta.identifier_exclusion
  (identifier_type, identifier_value_pattern, match_type, reason)
VALUES
  ('PHONE', '8005551212', 'EXACT', 'Corporate call center main line'),
  ('ANY', 'POS_GUEST_%', 'LIKE', 'Anonymous store register tokens');
  7. idr apply-config preserves manually inserted warehouse rows unless --reset is explicitly passed.

docs.title: 4. Manual Identity Stewardship Overrides (idr_meta.identity_override)
docs.text:
When automated rules need human-in-the-loop correction, stewards can define overrides via YAML (overrides:), the Web UI Cluster Explorer, dbt seeds (idr_overrides.csv), or direct SQL:

Override Type Effect on Graph Resolution FORCE_LINK Injects a synthetic edge between entity_key_a and entity_key_b so both records always resolve into the same cluster, even if they share zero identifiers. DO_NOT_LINK Removes any direct edge between entity_key_a and entity_key_b and detaches the higher entity key from any shared identifier anchor group containing both records. ISOLATE Strips all identifiers from entity_key_a prior to edge building so entity_key_a is guaranteed to remain a singleton cluster (resolved_id = entity_key_a). 
INSERT INTO idr_meta.identity_override
  (override_id, override_type, entity_key_a, entity_key_b, reason, created_by, is_active)
VALUES
  ('ov_vip_1', 'FORCE_LINK', 'crm:1001', 'orders:8842', 'Confirmed same customer by support ticket #492', 'steward@company.com', TRUE);

docs.title: 5. GDPR / CCPA Right-to-be-Forgotten (idr privacy forget)
docs.text: To comply with data deletion requests (GDPR Article 17 / CCPA), PrivacyManager (idr_core/privacy.py) purges an entity (or all entities matching an identifier value) across every IDR output and work table and writes a permanent compliance receipt into idr_meta.privacy_audit_log.

docs.title: CLI Usage
docs.text:
# Forget a specific entity key across all IDR output & work tables
idr privacy forget --platform duckdb --db demo.duckdb \
  --entity-key "crm:10042" \
  --reason "GDPR erasure request #REQ-2026-881" \
  --requested-by "privacy-team@company.com"

# Or forget all entities associated with an email/phone identifier value
idr privacy forget --platform duckdb --db demo.duckdb \
  --identifier-value "alice@example.com" \
  --identifier-type EMAIL \
  --reason "CCPA consumer deletion request"

docs.title: What Gets Purged & Logged
docs.text:
1. Resolves all target entity_key values and affected resolved_id clusters.
  2. Deletes matching rows from:
  3. idr_out.identity_resolved_membership_current
  4. idr_out.identity_identifiers_current
  5. idr_out.resolved_id_crosswalk
  6. idr_work.entities_delta, idr_work.identifiers_extracted, idr_work.identifiers_all, idr_work.entity_attributes, idr_work.edges_new, idr_work.lp_labels
  7. Recomputes or removes affected cluster summaries in idr_out.identity_clusters_current and idr_out.golden_profile_current.
  8. Inserts an immutable audit record (request_id, request_type, target_value, affected_entities_count, affected_clusters_count, tables_purged, requested_by, reason, executed_at, status) into idr_meta.privacy_audit_log.

docs.title: Getting Started & Installation
docs.text: sql-identity-resolution runs entirely inside your existing SQL data warehouse. Python (idr_core) compiles your declarative rules into dialect-native SQL statements executed directly by DuckDB, Snowflake, BigQuery, or Databricks.

docs.title: 1. Installation
docs.text:
Install the package with the extras matching your warehouse and desired interfaces:

All Extras (Recommended)DuckDB + Web UI + MCPSnowflakeBigQueryDatabricksFrom Source (Editable) 
pip install "sql-identity-resolution[all]"

pip install "sql-identity-resolution[duckdb,ui,mcp]"

pip install "sql-identity-resolution[snowflake]"

pip install "sql-identity-resolution[bigquery]"

pip install "sql-identity-resolution[databricks]"

git clone https://github.com/anilkulkarni87/sql-identity-oss.git
cd sql-identity-oss
pip install -e ".[all,dev]"

docs.title: Step 1: Run the Synthetic Demo (or Initialize Schemas)
docs.text:
To generate 10,000 realistic retail records across CRM, Orders, and POS tables and resolve them immediately in DuckDB:

idr quickstart --rows 10000 --output demo.duckdb

Or, if connecting to an existing database with your own source tables, initialize the idr_meta, idr_work, and idr_out schemas first:

idr init --platform duckdb --db demo.duckdb

docs.title: Step 2: Apply a Declarative Configuration YAML
docs.text:
Create a config.yaml file (or use examples/config_retail.yaml) and load it into idr_meta.*:

idr apply-config --platform duckdb --db demo.duckdb --config examples/config_retail.yaml

docs.title: Step 3: Execute the Resolution Pipeline
docs.text:
Run a full graph build (--mode FULL) or an incremental delta run (--mode INCR):

# First run: full graph resolution
idr run --platform duckdb --db demo.duckdb --mode FULL

# Subsequent runs: incremental watermark & state-diff resolution
idr run --platform duckdb --db demo.duckdb --mode INCR

[!TIP] Dry Run Preview: Add --dry-run to preview cluster merges, new entities, and largest cluster changes in idr_out.dry_run_results and idr_out.dry_run_summary without mutating production tables.

docs.title: Step 4: Launch the Interactive Web UI
docs.text:
Start the integrated FastAPI + React Web UI server:

idr ui --db demo.duckdb

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000 in your browser to:

  • Configure sources, canonicalizers, exclusions, and survivorship visually in the 6-Step Setup Wizard.
  • Trigger runs with a Live 8-Stage Execution Progress tracker.
  • Search entities, inspect confidence scores, create Manual Overrides (FORCE_LINK, DO_NOT_LINK, ISOLATE), or execute GDPR Erasure in the Cluster Explorer.

docs.title: 3. Zero-Config Credential Discovery
docs.text:
Both the CLI (idr) and the Web UI (idr ui) automatically discover local cloud credentials via idr_core/credential_discovery.py so you rarely need to type connection strings manually:

Warehouse Auto-Discovered Local Configs Environment Variables DuckDB Local *.duckdb files in the current workspace IDR_DATABASE (or --db) BigQuery ~/.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json & active gcloud project IDR_PROJECT / GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT, IDR_LOCATION Snowflake ~/.snowflake/connections.toml and ~/.snowflake/config SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT, SNOWFLAKE_USER, SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD, SNOWFLAKE_WAREHOUSE, SNOWFLAKE_DATABASE, SNOWFLAKE_ROLE Databricks ~/.databrickscfg profiles (HOST, token, http_path) DATABRICKS_HOST, DATABRICKS_TOKEN, DATABRICKS_HTTP_PATH, DATABRICKS_CATALOG

[!NOTE] Automatic --platform Detection: If you pass --db my_file.duckdb, --project my-gcp-project, or set IDR_PLATFORM, the idr CLI automatically resolves --platform for you.

docs.title: Interfaces: CLI, Web UI, FastAPI, MCP Server & dbt
docs.text: sql-identity-resolution provides five first-class interfaces that share the exact same underlying metadata model and graph resolution semantics.

docs.title: 1. Unified CLI Reference (idr)
docs.text: Command Description Example idr quickstart Generate synthetic retail data and run a complete local DuckDB resolution pipeline. idr quickstart --rows 10000 --output demo.duckdb idr init Initialize idr_meta, idr_work, and idr_out schemas and tables (--reset recreates them). idr init --platform duckdb --db demo.duckdb idr apply-config Compile and load a declarative YAML manifest into idr_meta.* tables. idr apply-config --db demo.duckdb --config config.yaml idr run Execute the 8-stage resolution pipeline (--mode FULL or --mode INCR, --dry-run, --strict). idr run --db demo.duckdb --mode INCR --max-iters 30 idr privacy forget Execute GDPR/CCPA right-to-be-forgotten erasure by --entity-key or --identifier-value. idr privacy forget --db demo.duckdb --entity-key crm:101 idr ui / idr serve Launch the FastAPI backend and bundled React Web UI (http://127.0.0.1:8000). idr ui --db demo.duckdb --port 8000 idr mcp Launch the FastMCP server for Claude Desktop, Cursor, and AI coding agents. idr mcp --db demo.duckdb idr dbt export Export YAML config or live warehouse idr_meta.* tables into the 7 dbt_idr seed CSVs. idr dbt export --file config.yaml --output-dir dbt_idr/seeds idr status Print recent pipeline runs and summary statistics from idr_out.run_history. idr status --db demo.duckdb idr inspect Inspect an entity key or cluster (resolved_id), its members, edges, and golden profile. idr inspect --db demo.duckdb --cluster crm:1

docs.title: 2. Interactive React Web UI (idr ui)
docs.text:
Launch the full-stack UI and API with a single command:

idr ui --db demo.duckdb

docs.title: Authentication Modes
docs.text:
• Local Development Mode (Default for idr ui):
  • When bound to a loopback address (127.0.0.1 / localhost), idr ui automatically enables IDR_ALLOW_INSECURE_DEV_AUTH=true, and the React SPA (IDRAuthProvider.tsx) activates local dev auth on loopback hosts when VITE_AUTH_AUTHORITY is not set.
  • Enterprise OIDC / JWT Mode (Production):
  • Set IDR_AUTH_ISSUER, IDR_AUTH_AUDIENCE, VITE_AUTH_AUTHORITY, and VITE_AUTH_CLIENT_ID (e.g., Keycloak, Okta, Auth0, Azure AD) to enforce Bearer JWT validation across all API routes.

docs.title: 6-Step Setup Wizard (/setup)
docs.text:
1. Connect (StepConnect): Auto-discovers local DuckDB files, gcloud ADC projects, ~/.snowflake/connections.toml, and ~/.databrickscfg profiles, or accepts custom warehouse credentials.
  2. Discover (StepDiscover): Scans schemas and tables in your warehouse with fuzzy search and row count previews.
  3. Map (StepMap): Auto-detects entity_key, watermark_column (updated_at, modified_at, order_date, event_ts, etc.), identifiers, and attributes per source table.
  4. Rules & Exclusions (StepRules):
  5. Configure deterministic rules with all 9 Domain Canonicalizers (EMAIL_STANDARD, EMAIL_STRIP_PLUS, PHONE_DIGITS, PHONE_US_10, ALPHANUMERIC_UPPER, LOWERCASE, UPPERCASE, EXACT/NONE) or a Custom SQL ({val}) expression input.
  6. Toggle Default Poison-Pill Exclusions (use_default_exclusions) and add custom EXACT/LIKE or ANY wildcard exclusions.
  7. Survivorship (StepSurvivorship): Configure PRIORITY, RECENCY, or FREQUENCY winners per profile attribute.
  8. Review & Run (StepReview):
  9. Above-the-Fold Action Bar & Run Configuration: Choose Incremental (Faster) or Full Refresh, Max Iterations, Strict Mode, or Dry Run and click Save Config or Run Pipeline without scrolling.
  10. Collapsible Summary Cards: Click Source Tables, Rules & Guardrails, Survivorship, or Raw JSON to inspect configuration details in bounded drawers.
  11. Live 8-Stage Execution Progress: Real-time progress bar (GET /api/setup/run/progress), elapsed timer, active stage indicator, and live Label Propagation iteration & label-change counter.

docs.title: Cluster Explorer & Stewardship (/explorer)
docs.text:
• Search by identifier value, entity_key, or resolved_id to inspect cluster graphs, confidence breakdowns, and Golden Profiles.
  • Stewardship Overrides Modal: Create or delete FORCE_LINK, DO_NOT_LINK, and ISOLATE overrides directly from the UI.
  • GDPR Forget Entity Modal: Purge an entity across all IDR tables with a single audited action.

docs.title: 3. FastAPI REST Endpoints (idr_api)
docs.text: Method & Path Description POST /api/connect Connect to DuckDB, Snowflake, BigQuery, or Databricks and initialize session lease. GET /api/setup/AutoConfig Reconstruct the full declarative configuration from idr_meta.* tables (sql_to_config). POST /api/setup/save Validate and apply configuration (config_to_sql) to idr_meta.*. POST /api/setup/run Execute the 8-stage IDRRunner in a background worker thread and return RunSummary. GET /api/setup/run/progress Poll non-blocking in-memory stage progress (stage_index, stage, iteration, changes, elapsed_seconds). GET /api/clusters/{id} Retrieve cluster members, connecting edges, confidence breakdown, and Golden Profile. GET /api/explorer/overrides List active manual stewardship overrides from idr_meta.identity_override. POST /api/explorer/overrides Create a FORCE_LINK, DO_NOT_LINK, or ISOLATE override. DELETE /api/explorer/overrides/{id} Deactivate a manual stewardship override. POST /api/explorer/forget Execute GDPR/CCPA erasure via PrivacyManager and return the audit receipt. GET /metrics Prometheus metrics endpoint (idr_entities_processed, idr_clusters_created, idr_run_duration_seconds).

docs.title: 4. FastMCP Server for AI Agents (idr mcp)
docs.text:
Expose your identity graph and configuration tools to Claude Desktop, Cursor, or any MCP client:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "sql-identity-resolution": {
      "command": "idr",
      "args": ["mcp", "--platform", "duckdb", "--db", "/absolute/path/to/demo.duckdb"]
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Exposed MCP Tools (idr_mcp/server.py)
docs.text:
• get_ClusterView(resolved_id) — Fetch cluster members, edges, confidence metrics, and golden profile attributes.
  • search_entities(query, limit) — Search entities across all identifier types and attributes.
  • explain_edge(entity_a, entity_b) — Explain which rules and normalized identifiers linked two entities.
  • list_runs(limit) & get_metrics() — Inspect pipeline run history, skipped identifier groups, and cluster size distribution.
  • configure_source(...), add_rule(...), run_pipeline(run_mode, dry_run) — Configure and run the pipeline via natural language.
  • export_dbt_seeds(output_dir, config_yaml) — Compile YAML or live warehouse metadata into dbt_idr seed CSVs.

docs.title: 5. dbt_idr Package Integration
docs.text: For teams that orchestrate transformations strictly through dbt Core or dbt Cloud, dbt_idr provides a pure-Jinja SQL implementation compatible with dbt-duckdb, dbt-snowflake, dbt-bigquery, and dbt-databricks.

docs.title: Exporting Config to dbt Seeds (idr dbt export)
docs.text:
You can design your rules in YAML or the Web UI and export all 7 standard dbt_idr seed CSVs in one command:

# Export from YAML file
idr dbt export --file examples/config_retail.yaml --output-dir dbt_idr/seeds

# Or export directly from a live warehouse's idr_meta.* tables
idr dbt export --platform duckdb --db demo.duckdb --output-dir dbt_idr/seeds

docs.title: Generated Seed Files (dbt_idr/seeds/)
docs.text:
1. idr_sources.csv — Source table coordinates, entity_key_column, and watermark_column.
  2. idr_identifier_mappings.csv — Source identifier columns (EMAIL, PHONE, LOYALTY, etc.).
  3. idr_attribute_mappings.csv — Source attribute mappings for survivorship.
  4. idr_rules.csv — Match rules, canonicalize strategy (EMAIL_STANDARD, EMAIL_STRIP_PLUS, PHONE_US_10, inline SQL {val}, etc.), and max_group_size.
  5. idr_exclusions.csv — Default and custom exclusions (including ANY wildcard patterns).
  6. idr_survivorship_rules.csv — PRIORITY, RECENCY, and FREQUENCY survivorship rules.
  7. idr_overrides.csv — Manual stewardship overrides (FORCE_LINK, DO_NOT_LINK, ISOLATE).

docs.title: Running dbt_idr
docs.text:
cd dbt_idr
dbt seed
dbt run
dbt test

docs.title: dbt_idr Model DAG
docs.text:
flowchart LR

docs.title: Supported Warehouses, Schema Reference & Operations
docs.text: sql-identity-resolution supports DuckDB, Snowflake, BigQuery, and Databricks with 100% feature parity across all 8 pipeline stages.

docs.title: 1. Warehouse Connection & Tuning Guide
docs.text:
DuckDBSnowflakeBigQueryDatabricks 
# Local file database
idr init --platform duckdb --db ./my_warehouse.duckdb
idr apply-config --db ./my_warehouse.duckdb --config config.yaml
idr run --db ./my_warehouse.duckdb --mode FULL
  • Best For: Local development, CI/CD testing, single-node analytics up to 50M+ rows.
  • Adapter: idr_core/adapters/duckdb.py (DuckDBAdapter).
export SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT="xy12345.us-east-1"
export SNOWFLAKE_USER="IDR_SERVICE_USER"
export SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD="..."
export SNOWFLAKE_WAREHOUSE="COMPUTE_WH"
export SNOWFLAKE_DATABASE="ANALYTICS"
export SNOWFLAKE_ROLE="IDR_ADMIN"

idr init --platform snowflake
idr apply-config --platform snowflake --config config.yaml
idr run --platform snowflake --mode INCR
  • Credential Auto-Discovery: Automatically reads ~/.snowflake/connections.toml and ~/.snowflake/config.
  • Adapter: idr_core/adapters/snowflake.py (SnowflakeAdapter).
# Authenticate via gcloud Application Default Credentials
gcloud auth application-default login

idr init --platform bigquery --project my-gcp-project --location US
idr apply-config --platform bigquery --project my-gcp-project --config config.yaml
idr run --platform bigquery --project my-gcp-project --mode INCR
  • Schema Mapping: Maps idr_meta, idr_work, and idr_out to BigQuery datasets in your target GCP project.
  • Adapter: idr_core/adapters/bigquery.py (BigQueryAdapter).
export DATABRICKS_HOST="adb-123456789.12.azuredatabricks.net"
export DATABRICKS_TOKEN="dapi..."
export DATABRICKS_HTTP_PATH="/sql/1.0/warehouses/abcdef123456"
export DATABRICKS_CATALOG="main"

idr init --platform databricks
idr apply-config --platform databricks --config config.yaml
idr run --platform databricks --mode INCR
  • Credential Auto-Discovery: Automatically reads ~/.databrickscfg profiles.
  • Table Existence Checks: Uses SHOW TABLES IN <schema> LIKE '<table_name>' so Unity Catalog / SQL Warehouses never log [TABLE_OR_VIEW_NOT_FOUND] errors during preflight checks.
  • Adapter: idr_core/adapters/databricks.py (DatabricksAdapter).

docs.title: 2. Complete Warehouse Schema Reference
docs.text: All tables are defined in idr_core/schema_defs.py (SYSTEM_TABLES) and mirrored in sql/ddl/{duckdb,snowflake,bigquery,databricks}.sql. During Stage 1 (preflight), PreflightStage._ensure_schema_upgrades() automatically creates any missing tables on existing deployments.

docs.title: idr_meta Schema (Configuration, State & Governance)
docs.text: Table Primary Key / Purpose Key Columns idr_meta.source_table Registered source tables table_id, table_fqn, entity_type, entity_key_expr, watermark_column, watermark_lookback_minutes, is_active idr_meta.source_identifier Identifier extraction mappings table_id, identifier_type, identifier_value_expr, is_hashed idr_meta.entity_attribute_mapping Profile attribute mappings table_id, attribute_name, attribute_expr idr_meta.rule Deterministic matching rules rule_id, identifier_type, canonicalize, max_group_size, priority, is_active idr_meta.fuzzy_rule Blocking-based fuzzy rules rule_id, rule_name, blocking_key_expr, score_expr, threshold, priority, is_active idr_meta.survivorship_rule Golden profile attribute rules attribute_name, strategy, source_priority_list, recency_field idr_meta.identifier_exclusion Poison-pill blocklist identifier_type (EMAIL, PHONE, ANY), identifier_value_pattern, match_type (EXACT, LIKE), reason idr_meta.identity_override Manual stewardship overrides override_id, override_type (FORCE_LINK, DO_NOT_LINK, ISOLATE), entity_key_a, entity_key_b, reason, created_by, is_active idr_meta.privacy_audit_log GDPR / CCPA erasure ledger request_id, request_type, target_value, affected_entities_count, affected_clusters_count, tables_purged, requested_by, reason, executed_at, status idr_meta.run_state Per-table incremental watermarks table_id, last_watermark_value, last_run_id, last_run_ts

docs.title: idr_work Schema (Ephemeral Pipeline Staging)
docs.text: Table Purpose idr_work.entities_delta New/updated entities extracted in the current run (watermark_value IS NOT NULL) plus candidate-expanded historical entities (watermark_value IS NULL). idr_work.identifiers_extracted Canonicalized and exclusion-filtered identifiers for current delta entities. idr_work.identifiers_all Full working set of identifiers across impacted entities used for anchor edge building. idr_work.entity_attributes Extracted attributes for fuzzy blocking (skipped automatically when 0 active fuzzy rules exist). idr_work.edges_new Anchor-based star edges ($N-1$ edges per group) after ISOLATE, DO_NOT_LINK, and FORCE_LINK overrides. idr_work.lp_edges / idr_work.lp_labels Undirected graph edges and iterative Label Propagation labels (stabilized against historical resolved_ids).

docs.title: idr_out Schema (Production Outputs & Telemetry)
docs.text: Table Purpose Key Columns idr_out.identity_resolved_membership_current Canonical mapping of every entity_key to its persistent resolved_id. entity_key, resolved_id, updated_at, super_cluster_id idr_out.identity_identifiers_current Current normalized identifiers per entity_key (powers candidate expansion & no-watermark state-diffing). entity_key, identifier_type, identifier_value_norm, is_hashed, updated_at idr_out.identity_clusters_current Cluster-level quality and confidence metrics. resolved_id, cluster_size, confidence_score, edge_diversity, match_density, primary_reason, updated_at idr_out.golden_profile_current Consolidated 360° customer profile per resolved_id. resolved_id, email_primary, phone_primary, first_name, last_name, <dynamic_attributes>, updated_at idr_out.resolved_id_crosswalk Historical ledger of cluster ID merges and splits across runs. run_id, old_resolved_id, new_resolved_id, entity_key, change_type, changed_at idr_out.run_history & idr_out.stage_metrics Run-level and stage-level execution telemetry. run_id, run_mode, status, entities_processed, edges_created, clusters_Impacted, lp_iterations, duration_seconds idr_out.skipped_identifier_groups Identifier groups skipped for exceeding max_group_size. run_id, identifier_type, identifier_value_norm, group_size, max_allowed, sample_entity_keys

docs.title: Recommended Incremental Scheduling Pattern
docs.text:
• Hourly / Intra-day Runs: Run idr run --mode INCR every 15–60 minutes. Watermarked event/order tables only scan rows newer than last_watermark_value, while dimension tables without watermarks use fast identifier state-diffing against idr_out.identity_identifiers_current and short-circuit immediately if no identifiers changed.
  • Weekly Guardrail Audit: Query idr_out.skipped_identifier_groups to spot new placeholder values that exceeded max_group_size and promote them to idr_meta.identifier_exclusion.

docs.title: Troubleshooting Common Scenarios
docs.text: Symptom Root Cause & Resolution Authentication Error in Local Web UI Always launch via idr ui (which sets IDR_ALLOW_INSECURE_DEV_AUTH=true on loopback hosts) or set VITE_ALLOW_INSECURE_DEV_AUTH=true if running Vite dev server directly. Incremental Run Re-Processes Unchanged Rows Ensure event/fact tables have a watermark_column mapped in sources:. For tables without a watermark_column, Stage 3 automatically diffs extracted identifiers against idr_out.identity_identifiers_current and prunes unchanged rows. Oversized Cluster Formed (cluster_size > 1000) Enable use_default_exclusions: true, inspect idr_out.skipped_identifier_groups, add the offending shared identifier to idr_meta.identifier_exclusion, or apply an ISOLATE / DO_NOT_LINK override in idr_meta.identity_override.

docs.title: Apache Airflow (deployment/airflow/)
docs.text: Automate hourly incremental and weekly full graph executions with pre-run safety gates: - Safety Gate: Runs idr run --mode INCR --dry-run and inspects idr_out.dry_run_summary (moved_entities, largest_proposed_cluster). If changes stay within configured thresholds, branches to live_incremental_run; otherwise aborts and notifies on-call. - Reference implementation: deployment/airflow/idr_dag.py.

docs.title: Snowflake Tasks & Streams (deployment/snowflake/)
docs.text: Schedule IDR and automate retention cleanup natively in Snowflake: - Incremental & Full Tasks: Runs hourly or weekly via Snowflake Tasks. - Daily Retention Cleanup: Purges idr_out.dry_run_results (7-day retention), idr_out.skipped_identifier_groups (30-day retention), and truncates ephemeral idr_work.* staging tables when no run is active. - Failure Alert Stream: An active stream on idr_out.run_history alerts immediately when status = 'FAILED'. - Reference implementation: deployment/snowflake/tasks.sql.

docs.title: BigQuery / GCP Terraform (deployment/gcp/)
docs.text: Provision serverless IDR pipelines on Google Cloud: - Creates idr_meta, idr_work, and idr_out BigQuery datasets. - Configures IAM service account with minimal roles/bigquery.jobUser and dataset permissions. - Deploys Cloud Function (2nd Gen) and Cloud Scheduler triggers for hourly incremental runs. - Reference implementation: deployment/gcp/main.tf.

docs.title: Enterprise Compose Stack with Keycloak SSO & Observability
docs.text:
Simulate or deploy production IDR with SSO, Redis session leasing, and metrics: 

docker compose -f docker-compose.enterprise.yml up -d --build
- Keycloak SSO: Bootstrapped via deployment/keycloak/idr-realm.json (test / test user). - Prometheus Metrics: Scrapes http://api:8000/metrics via monitoring/prometheus/prometheus.yml. - Grafana Dashboard: Pre-provisioned 6-panel dashboard (monitoring/grafana/dashboards/idr_dashboard.json) tracking entities processed, edges created, clusters impacted, and last run duration.

docs.title: Scale Testing & Benchmarking Tools (tools/scale_test/)
docs.text:
• End-to-End Benchmark: python tools/scale_test/run_scale_and_mcp_benchmark.py --rows 250000 --incr-rows 10000 (runs resolution, verifies 4 mathematical graph invariants, and benchmarks all MCP server tools).
  • Synthetic Omni-Channel Retail Generator: python tools/scale_test/generate_retail_idr_mimesis.py --config tools/scale_test/configs/retail_idr_5k.yaml (generates Parquet files across CRM, POS, E-commerce, web events, app events, and support tickets).
  • Cloud Loaders: Fast Parquet loaders for DuckDB (load_duckdb.py), BigQuery (load_bigquery.py), Snowflake (load_snowflake.py), and Databricks (load_databricks.py).
